stories.title: Bank of Canada raises benchmark rate to 2.5% to curb inflation risk from energy prices
stories.summary: On Oct. 28, the Bank of Canada lifted its benchmark interest rate by a quarter‑point to 2.5%, ending seven consecutive meetings at 2.25% and marking its first hike since July 2023. Governor Tiff Macklem said the increase is needed to lower the risk that high energy prices, which pushed September inflation to 3.1%, will spread to broader inflation. He added the rate remains low enough not to restrain growth and should help return inflation to target more quickly.
stories.why: Inflation data can shift expectations for central-bank interest rates, bond yields, borrowing costs and household purchasing power.

stories.title: Renfe high‑speed train collides with Iryo train after signalling error
stories.summary: At about 08:30 local time on a Wednesday, a Renfe high‑speed train carrying 397 passengers was ordered to proceed despite an automatic signalling computer failure that had stopped traffic on the Madrid‑Seville line. The train struck the rear of an Iryo private‑operator train with 147 passengers between the municipalities of Mora and Orgaz, roughly 140 km south of Madrid. Injuries reported included broken arms, broken noses and a rail that pierced a passenger’s roof.
stories.why: The incident shows how signalling failures and procedural mistakes can lead to serious accidents on high‑speed rail networks.

Several passengers suffered injuries, including broken arms, broken noses and a rail that penetrated a carriage roof.

stories.title: Microsoft recorded $10 billion in revenue from OpenAI
stories.summary: Microsoft generated $10 billion in revenue from commercial arrangements with OpenAI, including revenue-sharing payments, in the quarter ended September 30, the company said in a regulatory filing on Wednesday. (Microsoft’s financial year begins in July, making the quarter ended September 30, 2026 the first quarter of its fiscal 2027.) For the full 2026 fiscal year, revenue from OpenAI hit $24.1 billion.
stories.why: This matters because it could change AI capabilities, costs, adoption, regulation or competitive positioning.

stories.previousSummary: Microsoft generated $10 billion in revenue from commercial arrangements with OpenAI in the quarter ended September 30, 2026, representing nearly 11% of its $92.3 billion quarterly total. The company also reported $7.2 billion in outstanding receivables from OpenAI, up from $6 billion at end of June.

stories.title: Microsoft reports Azure revenue of $33.2 billion for Q3, up 48% YoY
stories.summary: Microsoft disclosed that Azure generated $33.2 billion in revenue for the July‑September quarter, a 48% increase from the same period a year earlier. The result topped analysts’ expectations by roughly $850 million and placed Azure slightly ahead of Google Cloud’s reported $30.7 billion for the quarter, enabling direct comparison with rivals such as Amazon Web Services.
stories.why: Direct dollar reporting lets investors benchmark Microsoft’s cloud business against competitors, affecting valuation and strategic assessments.
